D1.text: Every user-visible error is exactly one `line N: <message>` line, no traceback

D2.text: Evaluator is iterative for calls/blocks: user nesting depth never becomes Python stack depth

D3.text: Integer division/remainder truncate toward zero for negative operands

D4.text: REPL uses the exact prompt string and exits cleanly on EOF (Ctrl-D)

Q1.text: Conditions (if/while, and/or operands) must be booleans; non-boolean is a runtime error

Q2.text: `let` declares a new binding, `set` reassigns an existing one; bare assignment is a parse error

Q3.text: String concatenation is `~`; `+` on strings is a type error

Q4.text: Not-equals is `<>`; `!=` is a lex error

Q6.text: Comparisons do not chain (a < b < c is a parse error)

Q7.text: `and`/`or` never short-circuit; both operands are always evaluated

SC1.text: Python standard library only; no third-party packages

SC10.text: Every CLI entry point dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py

SC11.text: Line numbers surfaced to users are 1-indexed

SC12.text: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub in modules reachable from __main__ once a feature is claimed complete

SC2.text: Single-package layout: every module directly under bract/

SC3.text: All errors rendered through one shared error-formatting path

SC4.text: No print()/stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI module

SC6.text: Exit codes are exactly {0,1,2}, produced only by the CLI dispatch

SC7.text: No Python eval/exec/compile anywhere in bract/

SC8.text: No module-level mutable interpreter state; state threaded through an Interpreter/Environment

SC9.text: bract fmt only changes whitespace/indentation/brace placement, never AST

hints: why is my program printing extra output
does running a file echo expression values like the repl
bract run producing unexpected stdout
difference between repl and file execution output
req-05a5.statement: `bract run FILE` performs no implicit result-printing: it only emits whatever output the program itself writes, plus the single-line error message on failure — unlike the REPL, which echoes non-nil expression results.

hints: implementing bare assignment without let or set
should x = expr just work
set on an undeclared variable
walking the scope chain for reassignment
req-0ae3.statement: `set x = expr;` reassigns by walking the scope chain outward and fails with `line N: '<name>' is not declared` if no enclosing scope declared it; there is no bare `x = expr;` assignment form at all — omitting `let`/`set` is a parse error, not a binding operation.

hints: shadowing inside a plain block statement doesn't work
let inside a bare block leaks into the outer scope
redeclare error happens in a while loop but not in a plain block
double-nested scope after wrapping block evaluation in an extra Environment
req-0e7d.statement: Every block entered during evaluation — a bare `{ }` block statement, an if/else branch, or a while loop body — must get a freshly created child scope on entry, created once, uniformly, by the block-evaluation code itself rather than by each caller wrapping it in its own Environment.

hints: should = work as assignment like other languages
bare assignment statement
x = expr without set keyword
req-115c.statement: Bare assignment expressions like `x = expr;` (using `=` instead of the `set` statement) must be rejected by the parser, not accepted as a convenience alias for `set`.

hints: does the repl exit after a bad statement
error in interactive session should it crash
keep repl running after an exception
repl session ends unexpectedly on error
req-11e9.statement: An error raised while evaluating one REPL statement is reported via the shared 'line N: <message>' format but does not terminate the REPL session — the loop keeps reading and evaluating further statements.

hints: should this new module go in a subpackage
organizing bract source files
where do interpreter modules live
creating bract/core or bract/utils
req-15e3.statement: Every interpreter module lives directly under bract/ as a single flat package — no nested subpackages like bract/lexer/ or bract/core/parser/.

hints: can I use a pip package here
is it OK to add requests or another library
adding a dependency to requirements.txt
third-party library for parsing or regex
req-181b.statement: Bract is implemented in Python using the standard library only; no third-party package is ever imported, pip-installed, or listed in a dependency file.

hints: off-by-one in reported line number
is the first line of a file line 0 or line 1
line number mismatch between lexer and parser errors
req-1acd.statement: Line numbers reported in tokens, AST nodes, and error messages are 1-indexed everywhere; there is no 0-indexed line number anywhere in the pipeline.

hints: naming convention for token types
should token type be PascalCase or SCREAMING_CASE
adding a new token kind
req-2661.statement: Token type names in the lexer are SCREAMING_CASE (LET, IDENT, INT, STRING, TILDE, NOTEQ, etc.).

hints: REPL state leaking between sessions
why do tests interfere with each other
module-level dict for globals
singleton interpreter instance
req-274f.statement: Interpreter state (environments, call stacks, global bindings) must never live in module-level mutable variables; it belongs on instances of Interpreter/Environment created fresh per run.

hints: adding array or string indexing with brackets
s[0] syntax
subscript operator in the grammar
req-2ee2.statement: There is no subscript syntax (s[0]) anywhere in the Bract grammar; string indexing only exists via the at/sub builtins, so bracket-index parsing must not be added as a convenience.

hints: why does running a .bract file show nothing
where is the print or println builtin
program runs but produces no output
how do I print a value in bract
req-2f18.statement: Bract has no built-in print/output function; running a program via `bract run FILE` produces no output on its own; the only way values become visible is the REPL automatically echoing the result of each top-level expression statement.

hints: why isn't the repl printing my statement result
repl printing nil
does the repl echo every statement
repl output missing for a let statement
req-3eac.statement: In the REPL, only expression-statement results are printed, and only when the value is non-nil; other statement kinds and nil-valued expression statements print nothing.

hints: adding block comment support
/* */ comments in Bract
multi-line comment syntax
req-4923.statement: String concatenation is a `//` line comment only — there are no block comments in Bract.

hints: what does the repl prompt look like
trailing space after bract>
ctrl-d handling in the repl
EOFError in repl loop
repl exit code on eof
req-4adb.statement: The REPL prompt string is exactly 'bract> ' (with one trailing space), and EOF on stdin (Ctrl-D) ends the REPL session cleanly with exit code 0 rather than raising an uncaught exception.

hints: formatting an error message
how should this error look to the user
raising an exception for a parse or lex error
adding a new kind of runtime error
req-517b.statement: Every user-visible error (lex, parse, or runtime) is rendered as 'line N: <message>' via one shared error-formatting path, not ad hoc print/raise call sites.

hints: what error message for a bad escape sequence
unterminated string literal error
lexer error wording
req-5abd.statement: Bad string escapes produce `line N: unknown escape sequence '\x'` and an unterminated string produces `line N: unterminated string`, using the same shared line-numbered error format as all other lex/parse/runtime errors.

hints: chained comparisons a < b < c
should comparisons associate like Python
parsing a < b < c as (a<b)<c
req-6ee9.statement: The `comparison` grammar rule accepts at most one comp-op: chained comparisons like `a < b < c` must fail to parse with `line N: comparisons do not chain`, never silently associate left-to-right or right-to-left like Python's chained comparisons.

hints: adding a new kind of error
how do I report an error from a new module
stack trace showing up in output
which exception class should I raise
want to add a custom exception type
req-91a8.statement: Every lex, parse, and runtime error must be raised as a BractError subclass and rendered through bract/errors.py's format_error/print_error as a single 'line N: <message>' line on stderr — never a raw Python exception, a second line, or a traceback.

hints: writing or updating the README
should I copy the grammar into the README
docs task keeps saying see DESIGN.md
avoiding duplicate spec docs
why doesn't the README explain every operator
req-91d9.statement: User-facing docs (README) must not restate Bract's full grammar or semantics; point to DESIGN.md instead so the two documents cannot drift apart.

hints: if (1) throws a type error
using an integer as a condition
truthy falsy coercion in if statement
while loop condition type error
req-9484.statement: Conditions in `if`/`while` must be actual booleans; non-boolean values like integers are not coerced to truthy/falsy and produce a type error instead.

hints: formatter changes output every time it runs
fmt not idempotent
running fmt twice gives a different result
how to test formatter stability
req-9cd8.statement: `bract fmt` output must be byte-stable: formatting an already-formatted program is a no-op, i.e. fmt(fmt(x)) == fmt(x).

hints: off-by-one when calling at() or sub()
why does at(s,0) error
string slicing gives the wrong character
index out of range on first character
req-9db6.statement: The string builtins `at` and `sub` use 1-indexed positions, not the 0-indexed convention typical of Python/C-derived languages.

hints: relying on short-circuit to guard a bad expression
and/or side effects running twice
guard clause pattern like x != nil and x.foo() doesn't work
req-a15a.statement: `and` and `or` always evaluate both operands in Bract; there is no short-circuit evaluation.

hints: adding a new CLI entry point
should I create a separate script for a new subcommand
how are bract subcommands wired up
req-a2ee.statement: All CLI entry points (bract, bract run, bract fmt) must dispatch from a single bract/__main__.py; there is no second top-level script.

hints: shortcut using Python eval or exec
implementing a builtin by compiling Python
is it OK to use exec for the REPL
req-a9f2.statement: The interpreter must never call Python's eval, exec, or compile anywhere in the implementation -- Bract execution is a genuine tree-walking evaluation over the AST, not a delegation to the host Python runtime.

hints: should this function print directly
why can't the evaluator write to stdout
adding debug output inside a module
print statement inside the parser or lexer
req-b117.statement: No module other than the CLI entry point (bract/__main__.py) may call print, sys.stdout.write, or sys.stderr.write; all user-visible output funnels through that one module.

hints: formatter reordering expressions
does fmt change operator precedence
formatter altering the AST
is it safe for fmt to simplify parentheses
req-beac.statement: The formatter may only ever change whitespace, indentation, and brace placement; it must never reorder, re-associate, or drop AST nodes, and must exactly preserve expression grouping, operator precedence, and evaluation order.

hints: RecursionError on deep bract program
stack overflow on deeply recursive bract function
testing a 5000+ frame call chain
should function calls just use python recursion
maximum recursion depth exceeded running bract code
req-c4b1.statement: The evaluator must be fully iterative for function calls and block evaluation — no Python-stack recursion driven by user-input nesting depth; use an explicit stack/work-list instead of letting Bract call/block nesting recurse through Python's own call stack.

hints: let inside a while loop throws already declared on second iteration
does a loop body get a new scope each iteration
shadowing an outer variable from a nested block
redeclare error in a loop
req-d6c4.statement: A block's scope is created fresh on every entry: a `let` inside a `while` body or a function body declares a new binding on each iteration/call, not a redeclaration error. Redeclaring the same name within one and the same scope entry is `line N: '<name>' is already declared`; shadowing an outer binding from a nested inner scope is allowed.

hints: this is how Lox/Monkey does it so I'll follow that
assuming standard interpreter tutorial semantics
does Bract follow typical language conventions
req-da90.statement: DESIGN.md is the single source of truth for the Bract language and deliberately contradicts assumptions a typical Lox/Monkey/Python-style interpreter tutorial would make; read it before writing code rather than relying on priors from other toy-language implementations.

hints: negative number division gives a different result than python
should bract's / truncate or floor for negative operands
modulo sign convention for negative operands
implementing % with python's % operator
-7 / 2 what should this evaluate to
req-e6b4.statement: Integer division (`/`) and remainder (`%`) truncate toward zero for negative/mixed-sign operands, not floor — do not implement them with Python's own `/`/`//` or `%` operators directly, since those floor for negative operands.

hints: what exit code should a missing file give
exit code for file not found
should an IO error be exit 1 or 2
process exit code contract
unhandled exception reaching the cli
req-f55f.statement: Process exit codes are exactly 0 (success), 1 (runtime/evaluator error), and 2 (lex or parse error, including a missing input file or other pre-execution IO error) — no other value is ever returned, and the CLI boundary catches broadly so no Python traceback can reach a user-visible surface.

hints: found a TODO comment in the codebase
stub function with just pass
is this feature actually finished or a placeholder
leftover FIXME before release
req-f6bd.statement: No module reachable from bract/__main__.py may contain a leftover TODO/FIXME comment or a stub function body that's just `pass`; the polish/audit pass treats these as unfinished work, not acceptable shipping state.

hints: handling the != operator
should the parser accept bang-equals
user typed ! expecting logical not
not-equals syntax in Bract
req-f8d0.statement: There is no `!` token and no `!=` operator: a stray `!` produces `line N: unexpected character '!'`, not-equals is spelled `<>` (NOTEQ) instead, and `!=` is therefore unreachable at the parser — do not special-case `!=` anywhere.

hints: counter closure example returns wrong value
closure sees stale value after outer function returns
why does set work but let doesn't for the captured counter
chained calls f()() losing state
first-class function values and closures over let bindings
req-f932.statement: Closures must capture real references to outer bindings, not snapshots — a returned inner `fn` still sees, and can mutate via `set`, its outer `let` bindings after the outer function call has already returned.
